newsitem.title: USA: Cobalt price seen falling to $10 by 2000 - Roskill.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt price seen falling to $10 by 2000 - Roskill.

text.p: Global cobalt production could easily rise to 50,000 tonnes a year, with demand at 30,000 tonnes a year at best, although some planned projects will probably not go ahead, said Mark Seddon of metal market consultant Roskill.
"I would not be surprised to see cobalt prices down to about $10.00 a lb by the year 2000," he told delegates at the Gorham/Intertech conference in New York.
Seddon estimated the actual surplus around 2000 would be about 5,000 tonnes and noted the average price for cobalt in the past decade was about $10.
Seddon said 970 tonnes of fresh cobalt are due onstream next year, with the bulk of the projects starting up in 1998/99 and the huge Voisey's Bay project starting after 2000.

"Next year could still be quite interesting -- there won't be too much cobalt and demand will increase so there will be an equilibrium situation," he said. "But by the year 2000 cobalt prices are likely to weaken."
Delegates noted that another analyst, CRU International, forecast a cobalt price of $5.00 by 2005.
The majority of the new cobalt resources will come in the form of a by-product from nickel or copper projects.
